title: Create and edit a request
requirement: Requesters shall create requests (title, legal entity, currency, chart of account, requested for, organisation unit, project, need-by date, fiscal period, ship-to location, notes, custom fields, attachments) as Draft and edit them in Draft or Rejected; editing in other states is refused. The ship-to location defaults from the requester's purchasing profile (PUR-041).
acceptance_criteria: Given mandatory header fields, When saved, Then a Draft exists without a number.|Given a request in approval, When edited, Then it is refused with the state named. (error case)|Given a rejected request edited and resubmitted, When processed, Then a new approval chain is built.
notes: Was FF-050. The default ship-to comes from the eProcurement Suite's purchasing master since the review of L2 (ADR-0043).

title: Request lines and lots
requirement: Lines (item or free text, type product or service, quantity or amount basis, quantity, unit, unit price, currency, supplier suggestion, category, need-by, ship-to, custom fields) and lots with child lines, numbered per request, with a duplicate rule on item plus supplier plus account coding plus ship-to.
acceptance_criteria: Given a complete line, When saved, Then it gets the next line number and the request total updates.|Given a duplicate line, When saved, Then it is refused with the duplicate named. (error case)|Given a lot, When child lines are added, Then the lot total equals the sum of children.
notes: Was FF-051.

title: Account splits on lines
requirement: Each line shall be split across account strings with budget period and percent per the account split rule; a default split from the requester's organisation unit shall be proposed.
acceptance_criteria: Given splits of 60 and 40 percent, When submitted, Then validation passes.|Given splits totalling 90 percent, When submitted, Then "Allocations for line N total 90 percent; they must total 100" is shown. (error case)|Given a default split configured, When a line is created, Then it is pre-filled and editable.
notes: Was FF-052.

title: Line currencies and conversion
requirement: When multi-currency lines are allowed, lines may be in allowed currencies and are converted to the header currency with the rate valid on the request date; the request shows both amounts.
acceptance_criteria: Given a line in USD and header in INR, When saved, Then the converted amount uses the valid rate.|Given no rate, When saved, Then it is refused naming the pair and date. (error case)|Given multi-currency off, When editing, Then only the header currency is offered.
notes: Was FF-053.

title: Submission validations
requirement: On submit the system shall validate header mandatory fields, at least one line, mandatory line fields, splits totalling 100 percent, supplier status (published, not on hold, no critical flag, no blocking expired document), item status, budget period open, and run hook points; it shall then allocate the number and start the approval chain (or approve directly when no configuration applies).
acceptance_criteria: Given a complete request, When submitted, Then it is numbered and In Approval (or Approved).|Given a supplier on hold on a line, When submitted, Then it is refused naming the line and supplier. (error case)|Given a hook that blocks, When submitted, Then the message is shown and the request stays Draft.
notes: Was FF-054.

title: Budget check at submission
requirement: Submission shall apply the budget availability check with reservation (BF-065) when request budget validation is on, blocking or warning as configured, and show approvers the budget status per split.
acceptance_criteria: Given blocking on and budget short, When submitted, Then it is refused with the shortfall per account string. (error case)|Given warning on, When submitted, Then it proceeds and the approval screen shows the shortfall.|Given validation off, When submitted, Then no budget check runs and no reservation is made. (edge)
notes: Was FF-055. AC1 is marked as the error case it is (ADR-0041).

title: Approval of requests
requirement: Requests shall use the kernel workflow with the request document type, conditions on header, line and split fields (amount, category, legal entity, supplier, account string, custom fields), dynamic approvers (manager chain, budget owner, account string owner, category group) and the standard actions; approvers shall see lines, splits, budget status and attachments in the approval view.
acceptance_criteria: Given a configuration on amount above 10,000 with manager chain, When submitted, Then the requester's manager is an approver.|Given a rejection, When done, Then the requester is notified and may edit.|Given an approver who is also the requester and self-approval is disallowed, When they try, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: Was FF-056.

title: Cancel a request
requirement: The requester or a permitted user shall cancel a request in Draft, In Approval or Approved without orders, with a reason, releasing budget reservations and notifying pending approvers.
acceptance_criteria: Given an Approved request without orders, When cancelled, Then it is Cancelled and reservations released.|Given a request with an order, When cancelled, Then it is refused; close-short is offered instead. (error case)|Given cancellation, When audited, Then the reason is recorded.
notes: Was FF-057.

title: Request totals and summary
requirement: Requests shall show line totals, converted totals in header currency, tax estimate when codes are set, budget status per split, linked orders and a summary panel for approvers.
acceptance_criteria: Given lines in two currencies, When viewed, Then the total is in header currency with the rates used.|Given linked orders, When viewed, Then order numbers and statuses are listed.|Given no rate for a line, When totals compute, Then the total shows as unavailable with the reason instead of a wrong number. (error case)
notes: Was FF-063.

title: Convert a request to orders
requirement: A buyer shall convert an Approved request into one draft order per supplier (default) with the option to split or merge lines across orders before submission; lines without supplier must be assigned a supplier first; converted lines are linked and the request becomes Partially Ordered or Ordered.
acceptance_criteria: Given approved lines for two suppliers, When converted, Then two draft orders exist and the request is Ordered.|Given a line without supplier, When converted, Then it is refused naming the line. (error case)|Given only some lines converted, When saved, Then the request is Partially Ordered with remaining quantities visible.
notes: Was FF-058. The buyer converts on Orders' screen, which reads the approved lines through this product's Contracts and marks them converted, so the request becomes Partially Ordered or Ordered at once (ADR-0042). Decision F-01 confirmed.

title: Partial ordering and close-short
requirement: Remaining quantities on request lines shall be orderable later; a buyer or requester shall close a request or line short with a reason, releasing remaining budget reservation.
acceptance_criteria: Given a line of 10 with 6 ordered, When viewed, Then 4 remains orderable.|Given close-short, When applied, Then the remaining 4 is released and the line is Closed.|Given a closed line, When conversion is attempted, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: Was FF-059.

title: Buyer and work queue from the purchasing group
requirement: A request line's buyer shall be a buyer of the purchasing group that serves the line's category and unit (PUR-001), and a buyer's work queue of approved lines to order shall show the lines of the groups they belong to, filterable by group.
rationale: Buyers work by what they buy and for whom; the purchasing group says which buyer a line goes to.
acceptance_criteria: Given a purchasing group covering IT hardware for unit A, When a request line of IT hardware in unit A is approved, Then a buyer of that group is its buyer.|Given a buyer of two purchasing groups, When they open their work queue, Then it shows the approved lines of both groups and can be filtered by group.|Given a line whose category and unit no purchasing group serves, When it is approved, Then it has no buyer and the queue shows it as unassigned. (error case)
notes: New at the review of the PRD split, 2026-10-20: purchasing groups assign the buyer and filter the work queue (PUR-001, BF-007 until the review of L2 moved it to the eProcurement Suite's purchasing master). They give no access, so a buyer still needs a role over the line's unit to open it.

title: Copy and templates
requirement: Users shall copy a request into a new draft and save requests as personal or shared templates; templates pre-fill header and lines without numbers.
acceptance_criteria: Given a copy, When created, Then lines and splits are copied as a new Draft.|Given a template used, When created, Then the request is Draft with template lines.|Given a template with an inactive item, When used, Then the line is flagged for review. (edge)|Given a template shared by a user without the share permission, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: Was FF-060. Decision F-12 confirmed.

title: Request lists and visibility
requirement: Lists of requests with filters (status, requester, unit, period, supplier, amount) shall respect visibility: requesters see their own and those requested for them, buyers see their units, approvers see those they act on, administrators see all.
acceptance_criteria: Given a requester, When listing, Then only their requests appear.|Given a buyer scoped to unit A, When listing, Then requests of unit A and children appear.|Given a user without any request permission, When opening, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: Was FF-061.

title: Operational reports
requirement: The reports in section 11.3 shall be available as grids with filters, saved views and export, respecting permissions and visibility.
acceptance_criteria: Given a user without the reports permission, When opening, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given export, When run, Then the file matches the grid.
notes: Was FF-160, the request reports; the others are ORD-081, RCV-101, INV-084 and CAT-041. Placed by the test: each product owns its reports.

title: Notification keys of Requests
requirement: Requests shall declare its notification keys on the business layer's notification templates (BF-164), each with the event that raises it, the placeholders it offers, its default audience and an English starter template: request approved and request rejected (the requester, REQ-007), request cancelled (the requester, REQ-008), line assigned (the buyer, REQ-023) and request recorded on your behalf (the person it is for, REQ-122).
rationale: The product knows what happens to its documents; the tenant decides, in its own words, who hears of it (BF-164). A suite's keys and starter templates are the suite's content (ADR-0043).
acceptance_criteria: Given a tenant with the eProcurement Suite, When it is provisioned, Then each key of Requests exists with its English starter template and its default audience.|Given a request rejected (REQ-007), When the rejection is saved, Then the requester is told in the key's template.|Given a starter template that names a placeholder its key does not offer, When the module's declarations are checked at start, Then the start fails naming the key and the placeholder. (error case)
notes: Was BF-164, the keys and starter templates of Requests. Moved at the review of L2, 2026-10-20 (ADR-0043): each product declares its keys and starter templates; BF-164 keeps the mechanism. Changed 2026-10-21 at SUP-gaps' review: the requirements that raise its keys in a later slice (REQ-023, with Orders) depend on this declaration, not the reverse, so no requirement depends on one of a later slice (`make prd-check`). Changed 2026-10-30 (EPS-modules): the key "request recorded on your behalf" (REQ-122).

title: Request types: one front door for every purchase need
requirement: Every purchase need shall start at one front door, where the requester first chooses what they need, its request type: a catalogue item, free-text goods, services, software, or contractors, the five types the eProcurement Suite brings. The type decides the questions the requester answers, a form of the forms engine (TF-242) attached to the request; the line fields that are required (a service line by amount and period, a software line with its number of users and its term); and the reviews that may apply (REQ-102). A catalogue item request takes its lines from the catalogue's cart where Catalogue is licensed (CAT-021); the other types have free-text lines guided by their questions. A tenant may deactivate a type, change its questions, and add types of its own, each based on one of the five.
rationale: A requester should not have to know which process applies to what they buy: software needs a security review, a contractor legal and onboarding checks, a catalogue item none. One front door that asks the right questions for the type routes every need, and it is what the leading suites now sell as intake.
acceptance_criteria: Given the five request types active, When a requester starts a request, Then they choose its type first, and the questions of that type's form are shown.|Given a software request whose form asks whether the software will hold personal data, When the requester answers yes, leaves the question on the kinds of data empty and submits, Then it is refused naming the question. (error case)|Given a request type the tenant deactivated, When a requester starts a request of that type through a saved link or the API, Then it is refused naming the type. (error case)|Given a tenant's own type based on services, When a line is added to a request of that type, Then it is a service line by amount and period.
notes: New 2026-10-30 (EPS-modules), the owner's decision of 2026-10-29 (ADR-0058): intake as one front door for any purchase need, by request type. The five types and their forms are the suite's content (ADR-0043, decision 8). Decision, proposed default: a tenant's own types are each based on one of the five, so that the line fields and the routing that follow from a type stay known; the type is chosen once, and a different type means a new request, since the form and the reviews depend on it.

title: Reviews by type and value before ordering
requirement: A submitted request shall go through the reviews its type, its value and its form's answers call for, before any of its lines can be ordered: legal (for example when the supplier asks for its own terms to be signed), security or IT (software, and services that touch the tenant's data or systems), finance (above a value the tenant sets, or a line without budget), and procurement (above a value the tenant sets, or a supplier not yet approved). Each review is a step of the request's approval on the kernel's workflow (REQ-007, TF-090), configured per request type with conditions on the amount, the category and the form's answers, its reviewers resolved like any approver (TF-091); reviews that do not wait for each other run at the same time. A reviewer sees the request, its form and its lines, and approves, rejects with a reason, or returns the request with questions; the request is approved only when every review that applies has approved. The suite's approval starter set (PUR-061) holds one inactive example per request type.
rationale: Legal, security and finance reviews that happen after the order is placed come too late, and reviews that every request goes through waste everyone's time. Routing them by type, value and answers, before ordering, asks each team only about what it must see.
acceptance_criteria: Given a configuration that sends software to security or IT, When a software request is submitted, Then the security or IT review is a step of its approval, and the request is not approved until that review approves.|Given a services request of 60,000 whose form says the supplier asks for its own terms, and a configuration with legal on that answer and finance above 50,000, When it is submitted, Then the legal and the finance reviews run at the same time, and the request is approved only when both have approved.|Given a review that rejects with a reason, When the rejection is saved, Then the request is Rejected and the requester sees the reviewer's reason.|Given a configuration whose legal review resolves no reviewer for the request's unit, When the request is submitted, Then it is refused naming the review and the missing reviewer, and the request stays Draft. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-30 (EPS-modules), the owner's decision of 2026-10-29 (ADR-0058): reviews routed by type and value to legal, security or IT, finance and procurement, before ordering. Decision, proposed default: the starter examples, inactive until an administrator activates them (PUR-061): software, security or IT always, and legal when the form says terms must be signed; services and contractors, legal when terms must be signed, and procurement above 10,000 in the legal entity's currency; free-text goods, procurement above 10,000; any type, finance above 50,000 or with a line without budget; catalogue items, nothing beyond the approval REQ-007 runs. The values are examples an administrator changes before activating them.

title: The buying model as configuration
requirement: The tenant shall set its buying model per legal entity, unit and category: desktop buying, where everyone who may raise requests raises their own, catalogue and contract lines are ordered automatically where the rules allow (REQ-142), and the other approved lines go to the buyers, who consolidate them into orders (REQ-161); central buying, where the buying desk buys for everyone, a setting decides who may raise requests (REQ-122), and every approved line goes to the buyers; or the mix, by giving some units or categories a model other than their legal entity's. The default, for a tenant that sets nothing, is desktop buying with consolidation at the buying desk. The model that applies to a request line is the most specific one set: for the line's category in the request's unit or the nearest unit above it, then for the category at the legal entity, then for the unit or the nearest unit above it, then for the legal entity, then the tenant's default. A request shows each line's model and where it came from.
rationale: Groups buy differently in different places: a head office buys IT centrally while its plants let people order their own supplies, and a category such as IT may be bought centrally everywhere. A model in configuration, rather than a fork in the product, lets one tenant run all of them.
acceptance_criteria: Given a tenant that has set no buying model, When a request line is added, Then desktop buying applies to it.|Given legal entity L on desktop buying and its unit U on central buying, When a person of U adds a request line, Then central buying applies to it, from unit U.|Given unit U on desktop buying and the category IT hardware on central buying at legal entity L, When a line of IT hardware is added to a request of U, Then central buying applies to it, from the category at L.|Given unit U on central buying where only nominated people may request, with no nominated requester and no buyer of a purchasing group serving U, When the model is saved, Then it is refused naming the unit, since nobody could raise its requests. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-30 (EPS-modules), the owner's decision of 2026-10-29 (ADR-0058): desktop buying, central buying or the mix, as configuration per legal entity, unit and category, desktop buying with consolidation at the buying desk by default. Decision, proposed default: a category's model comes before a unit's, since a category bought centrally is usually bought so everywhere; within each, the nearest unit up the tree wins; under central buying, automatic orders are off unless the tenant allows them there too (REQ-142).

title: Who may request under central buying, and requests on behalf
requirement: Under central buying, a setting of the model shall decide who may raise requests: everyone who holds the permission to create requests, or only the unit's nominated requesters and the buyers of the purchasing groups that serve it (PUR-001). A buyer shall record a request that arrived outside the system, by email, telephone or on paper, on behalf of the person or unit that needs it, with the original attached as evidence (TF-160); the request names the person or unit it is for and the buyer who recorded it, follows the same validations and approvals as if that person had raised it, and its person is told that it was recorded (REQ-081).
rationale: Central buying means a buying desk that buys for others, and much of its demand still arrives by email and telephone; recording it on behalf, with the evidence, puts that demand under the same control as the rest.
acceptance_criteria: Given unit U on central buying where only nominated people may request, When a person who is neither nominated nor a buyer serving U starts a request for U, Then it is refused, and the message names the buying desk to send the need to. (error case)|Given an email from a person of U asking for 20 chairs, When a buyer records the request on behalf of that person with the email attached, Then the request is for that person, names the buyer as who recorded it, and its approval resolves that person's manager, not the buyer's.|Given a request recorded on behalf with neither an original attached nor a note of a call, When it is submitted, Then it is refused naming the missing evidence. (error case)|Given a request recorded on behalf of a person, When it is saved, Then that person is told in the key "request recorded on your behalf" and finds it among their requests (REQ-042).
notes: New 2026-10-30 (EPS-modules), the owner's decision of 2026-10-29 (ADR-0058): central buying, who may request, and requests recorded on behalf with the original as evidence. Decision, proposed default: the original is required, and a need given by telephone or in person is recorded with a note naming who asked and when in its place; recording on behalf takes the permission `requests.requests.record_on_behalf`, which the buyers' role holds.

title: Demand imported in bulk
requirement: A buyer shall import demand in bulk through the kernel's import (TF-205): a file of request lines, each naming the person or unit it is for, the item or its description, the quantity and unit, the need-by date, the ship-to and the account split. Each row is validated as a line entered by hand is (REQ-002, REQ-003); the valid rows become requests on behalf (REQ-122), one per person or unit and legal entity, each recorded as the buyer's with the file attached as its evidence. They are created in Draft, and the buyer submits them, together or one by one; from then on they are approved, routed and consolidated like any other request.
rationale: Central buying often collects demand in a spreadsheet, a season's uniforms or a year's stationery; importing it keeps the buyer from typing hundreds of lines, and keeps each line's requester, split and evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Given a file of 300 rows for 12 units of one legal entity, When it is imported, Then 12 draft requests on behalf exist, one per unit, each with the file attached.|Given a file with 3 rows whose splits total 90 percent, When it is previewed, Then those rows are listed with the reason and the others can proceed. (error case)|Given a person without the permission to record requests on behalf, When they import demand, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-30 (EPS-modules), the owner's decision of 2026-10-29 (ADR-0058): demand imported in bulk through the kernel's import, and consolidated like any other. Decision, proposed default: one request per person or unit and legal entity, created in Draft for the buyer to submit, so that a large file is checked before anyone's approval starts. A demand that recurs is the recurring request section 2.2 leaves for later.

title: Routing rules for approved lines
requirement: When a request is approved, each of its lines shall be routed by the tenant's routing rules, and the line shows its route and why: a line from a catalogue or contract item, with its supplier and price known, to an automatic order where the automatic order rules allow it (REQ-142); any other line, to the work queue of its buyer (REQ-023); and a line above the sourcing limit, to sourcing first. Two limits are set per legal entity in its currency, and may be set per category: lines up to the first go to the buyer's queue as they are; lines between the two go to it marked "quotations advised"; lines above the second, the sourcing limit, must be sourced first. With Sourcing (wave 2) such a line becomes a sourcing need; until then it goes to its buyer's queue flagged "source first", naming the limit, and an order made from it keeps the buyer's reason for not sourcing it (ORD-161). A line without a supplier always goes to the buyer's queue.
rationale: A buyer's time belongs where a buyer is needed. Lines whose supplier and price are agreed need none; small free-text lines need an order; large ones need competition before a supplier is chosen.
acceptance_criteria: Given limits of 10,000 and 100,000 at legal entity L, When a request of L with free-text lines of 4,000, 40,000 and 400,000 is approved, Then the first goes to its buyer's queue, the second to the queue marked "quotations advised", and the third to the queue flagged "source first" naming the limit.|Given a tenant that has set no limits, When a request is approved, Then every line not ordered automatically goes to its buyer's queue without a mark.|Given the category IT hardware with a sourcing limit of 50,000 of its own at L, When a line of IT hardware for 60,000 is approved, Then it is flagged "source first" naming the category's limit.|Given a sourcing limit lower than the first limit, When it is saved, Then it is refused naming both limits. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-30 (EPS-modules), the owner's decision of 2026-10-29 (ADR-0058): catalogue and contract lines to automatic orders, other lines below a limit to the buyer's queue, lines above a higher limit sourced first, flagged to the buyer until Sourcing exists. Decision, proposed defaults: between the two limits a line goes to the buyer's queue marked "quotations advised", a mark for the buyer and the reports that does not block the order; no limit is set until the tenant sets one; a category's limit comes before its legal entity's. A line routed to sourcing is Sourcing's to handle once that module's PRD is written; this requirement routes it and depends on nothing of Sourcing's.

title: Automatic orders
requirement: An approved request line shall become an order without a buyer when the automatic order rules of its legal entity allow it: the line comes from a catalogue item or a contract item (CAT-021, CAT-022), so its supplier and price are known; its category is one the rules enable; its amount is within the rules' limit for that category; and its supplier is one the rules enable for automatic orders and is enabled in the line's organisation (BF-108). Requests then publishes the line as ready for an automatic order, an event Orders handles (ORD-162); a line that fails a rule goes to its buyer's queue naming the rule. Automatic orders apply where the buying model is desktop buying (REQ-121), and under central buying only where the tenant allows them there too.
rationale: Under desktop buying most lines are catalogue and contract items whose supplier and price are already agreed; ordering them without a buyer is what makes desktop buying fast, and the rules keep it to what the tenant trusts.
acceptance_criteria: Given a rule at legal entity L enabling office supplies up to 2,000 and supplier S, and an approved catalogue line of office supplies for 300 from S, When the request is approved, Then the line is published as ready for an automatic order and no buyer is assigned to it.|Given the same rule and an approved catalogue line of office supplies for 2,500 from S, When the request is approved, Then the line goes to its buyer's queue naming the limit it exceeded.|Given an approved free-text line with a suggested supplier and price, When the request is approved, Then it is not ordered automatically and goes to its buyer's queue.|Given a unit on central buying where the tenant has not allowed automatic orders, When an approved catalogue line within the rules is routed, Then it goes to its buyer's queue naming the buying model.|Given a rule that enables a supplier enabled in no organisation of its legal entity, When the rule is saved, Then it is refused naming the supplier. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-30 (EPS-modules), the owner's decision of 2026-10-29 (ADR-0058): an approved line from a catalogue or a contract, with a known supplier and price, becomes an order without a buyer, by rules on the category, an amount limit and the suppliers enabled. An automatic conversion is an event (ADR-0042, decision 4). Decision, proposed defaults: the suppliers enabled for automatic orders are named in these rules rather than on the supplier's purchasing profile, so the purchasing master is unchanged; under central buying automatic orders are off unless the tenant allows them; a legal entity without rules has no automatic orders.

title: Consolidation across requests by a buyer
requirement: A buyer's work queue (REQ-023) shall offer the approved lines of many requests together, grouped by supplier, legal entity, currency and payment terms, and let the buyer select lines from any number of requests and order them in one step: Orders' screen reads the selected lines through this product's Contracts and makes one order per group (ORD-161), and each line is marked converted, linked to its order line, at once, so that each request becomes Partially Ordered or Ordered as REQ-021 says. Each line keeps its own account split, ship-to and need-by date on its order line.
rationale: Ten requests for one supplier in a week should reach it as one order, not ten: fewer orders and invoices, and better prices. The default buying model consolidates at the buying desk.
acceptance_criteria: Given approved lines of three requests for supplier S at legal entity L, in one currency and on the same terms, When the buyer selects them and orders them, Then one draft order to S holds the three lines, each linked to its request line, and each request is Ordered or Partially Ordered.|Given selected lines for supplier S from two legal entities, When they are ordered together, Then two orders are made, one per legal entity.|Given a selected line that another buyer ordered a moment before, When the buyer orders the selection, Then it is refused naming that line, and nothing of the selection is ordered. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-30 (EPS-modules), the owner's decision of 2026-10-29 (ADR-0058): a buyer selects approved lines from many requests in the work queue and creates one order per supplier. An order has one legal entity, currency and set of payment terms, so a group is one supplier with one of each; decision F-01 (the buyer may split or merge before submitting) holds. The buyer converts on Orders' screen, a call into this product (ADR-0042, decision 4).

title: Automatic consolidation over a window
requirement: Lines ready for automatic orders (REQ-142) shall be collected over a window the tenant sets per legal entity and, when the window closes, published together in groups that share supplier, legal entity, currency and payment terms, so that Orders makes one order per group (ORD-163) rather than one per request. The window is a schedule of closing times in the legal entity's time zone on its working days (TF-099), or none, when each line is published at once. A line whose need-by date falls before the next close is published at once, alone; a line cancelled while it waits (REQ-008) is not published.
rationale: Desktop buying makes many small automatic orders; collecting a day's lines turns a supplier's twenty orders into one, as a buyer consolidating by hand would, without a buyer.
acceptance_criteria: Given a daily window closing at 16:00 and three requests approved at 09:00, 11:00 and 15:00 with automatic lines for supplier S at legal entity L, in euros on net 30 days, When the window closes, Then the three lines are published as one group, and none was published before.|Given automatic lines for S on two different payment terms, When the window closes, Then they are published as two groups.|Given a window closing on Fridays and an automatic line approved on Tuesday with a need-by date of Thursday, When the request is approved, Then the line is published at once, alone.|Given a window schedule with no closing time, When it is saved, Then it is refused naming the schedule. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-30 (EPS-modules), the owner's decision of 2026-10-29 (ADR-0058): automatic consolidation collects lines that share supplier, legal entity, currency and terms over a window the tenant sets. Decision, proposed default: on, daily, closing at 16:00 in the legal entity's time zone on its working days, so a day's lines for a supplier reach it as one order that afternoon; "none" publishes each line at once. The outbox (TF-085) publishes each group once.

title: Each requester follows their own line
requirement: A request line ordered by any path, a buyer's conversion (REQ-021), a consolidation (REQ-161, REQ-162) or an automatic order (REQ-142), shall keep the order line it became, which Orders writes through this product's Contracts when it marks the line converted, and its requester shall open that order line from their request to follow the order, its receipts and its delivery. Where identical lines became one order line (ORD-164), the request line names its own share, with its quantity and account split. A requester sees their own line and share through it, and never another requester's request.
rationale: Consolidation must not cost the requester their view: whoever asked for something follows it to delivery, however many other requests share its order.
acceptance_criteria: Given a request line ordered in one order with lines of two other requests, When its requester opens their request, Then the line shows its order number and order line, and opens it.|Given identical lines of requesters A and B made one order line of 30, A's share 10, When A opens their request, Then the line shows the order line and A's share of 10 with A's account split.|Given the same order line, When A asks for B's request by its identifier, Then it is refused, as REQ-042 refuses it.
